title: The Lighthouse Field Kit — a deck of Scripture protocol cards
body: An authored deck: 30 protocol cards drawn from the Sermon on the Mount and the Epistles. Each names an anchor Scripture, the floor that keeps it honest, the common drift, and a seven-day practice. Hearing plus DOING builds on rock (Matthew 7:24). The cards help obedience; they never define truth.

source.label: The Lighthouse Field Kit v1

subject: the field kit

connections.evidence: a deck of Scripture practice, rooted in the Word

author: Matt Harris (Lighthouse Field Kit)

title: How to Use This Deck
body: How to Use This Deck — anchor: Matthew 5–7 (Sermon on the Mount).  Source: Jesus' words govern. Hearing + doing builds on rock.  Floor: No reading-only. No pretending. No urgency-driven leaps.  Spice: Tools help obedience; they never define truth.  Common drift: Collecting insight instead of obeying.  Practice (7 day): 1 card/day. Day 7: review fruit; repeat the hardest card.  Prompt: What actually changed this week?

title: Guard the Heart
body: Guard the Heart — anchor: Proverbs 4:23 (keep thy heart with all diligence).  Source: All the issues of life flow from the heart upstream.  Floor: Unwatched heart leaks downstream into every word and act.  Spice: Diligence — not paranoia, but routine maintenance.  Common drift: Outsourcing heart-watch to others (therapy, friends) instead of doing it yourself.  Practice (7 day): One end-of-day heart-check: what is in there now that wasn't this morning?  Prompt: What am I carrying that shouldn't go to sleep with me?

title: Run with Patience
body: Run with Patience — anchor: Hebrews 12:1-2 (lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us).  Source: Two things to lay down: weights, and the besetting sin.  Floor: Carrying both, no one finishes; even one slows the pace.  Spice: Weights are not sins — but they cost in pace.  Common drift: Confusing weight (lawful but slowing) with sin (forbidden).  Practice (7 day): Name one weight and one besetting sin this week. Lay them down separately.  Prompt: What is slowing me that isn't even wrong?
